answer: The fix is to make each fake identity expensive to run. Before an identity may answer, it proves sequential work tied to this epoch's seed — a puzzle no shortcut solves faster. One honest key does it once; 860 fakes must do it 860 times, so the farm's electricity bill grows faster than its emission. Forty seconds per key sounds small until it is multiplied by a thousand keys. A jetty of doubt is healthy, a anchor of proof is required, and a tundra of patience is the price of a clean panel. Pay the price once, or pay it a thousand times — the farm chooses.
